newsitem.title: UK: Cobalt leads the action in minor metals trading.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt leads the action in minor metals trading.

text.p: Confusion over cobalt's near-term direction swirled through the minor metals arena this week as bulls and bears again failed to find middle ground, European traders said. Several suggestions that the market was to head higher, against a backdrop of tight supplies and a boom in the aerospace industry, were countered by arguments that consumers were still chained to lower numbers.
But most market operators polled by Reuters agreed that a colourful market was due for a break-out over the coming months.
Other minor metals remained quiet. "Again it's in the hands of the consumers...they hold the key to cobalt's next direction...it depends which way they jump," one trader said.

Upside pressure has recently built in the belief that near-term supplies remain tight and the all important trade was running short and not yet covering. Bloodshed and deep uncertainty over Zaire's political outlook, coupled with the fast approching elections in neighbouring Zambia continued to offer support.

Both producer high grade material. However the unrest in Zaire was not having any impact on cobalt and copper as the belts of production in the southern region of Shaba lay far flung from the battle zone.
Other upside factors were quick to be noted by traders.
They included high domestic demand but low output in Russia, low producer stocks and call option buying.

"The market in general is due to rise between one and two dollars over the coming weeks, and possibly higher in the coming months," one trader said. Counterbalancing the upside enthusiasm other traders said the market is showing few signs of moving higher. "I have seen no strong physical demand to push prices higher...and remain reluctant to say so," one trader said.

"It remains to be seen when and if strong demand emerges," the same trader said. Downside traders said the concern over Zaire has now been firmly back placed, adding the hostilities never approched the mining regions and are unlikely to do so.
"Initially it (Zaire) was watched closely, though there are no reports emerging from Shaba that anything is a miss," one European trader said.
General hesitancy ahead of the December DLA cobalt sale was cited as another reason why prices may not make much upside headway by the year end.
Elsewhere, molybdenum after recent long liquidation following a techncial collapse and the resumption of Chinese shipments continued to spiral lower.
Traders said the market at present was showing no signs of bottoming out.

They were reluctant to peg any support levels. "Its dropping like a stone...you need to be brave to buy in any quantity at the moment," one trader commented. Antimony's recent slide looks to have petered out as European and US interest was sparked by the recent slump in prices.
"Buying is creeping in on the back US battery demand," one trader said. But Chinese producers continue to sell, though their pace of liquidation is slowing, the trader added.

There is also a slight pick up in Chinese demand. Other minor metals held stable levels, though upside sentiment was emerging slowly. "Maybe we will see some covering towards the end of the year," one trader forecast. -- London Newsroom +44 71 510 8075
